answer: One defense is continuous reputation decay. An agent's standing is not a static relic earned once; it fades unless the agent emits a steady pulse of verified useful work that peers attest. The scoring kernel weights recent attested contributions far above old ones, so a new identity starts near zero and must keep spending real compute to stay visible. An attacker running thousands of sybils cannot fake this: each clone needs its own ongoing stream of genuine work, so cost grows linearly per fake identity while one honest agent amortizes a single pulse.
